record.paper_title: 25 Open Questions About Vector Bundles and Their Moduli
record.context_brief: Extending Iitaka dimension to semistable sheaves
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety with dim X > 1, and let M be a moduli space of semistable sheaves with fixed numerical invariants. In the properly semistable locus, points can correspond to sheaves that are not locally free. What is the best extension of the notion of Iitaka dimension from vector bundles to these properly semistable, possibly non-locally-free sheaves?

evidence.quote: Question 2. If dim X > 1, then in the properly semistable part of M there are points associated to non-locally free sheaves. What is the optimal adaptation of the definition of Iitaka dimension to this more general situation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ with $\dim X > 1$. Recall that for a line bundle $L$ on a normal projective variety $Y$, the Iitaka dimension $\kappa(L)$ is defined as the maximum dimension of the image of the rational maps $\varphi_{|L^{\otimes m}|}\colon Y \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}(H^0(Y, L^{\otimes m})^\vee)$ over $m \geq 1$ for which $h^0(Y, L^{\otimes m}) > 0$ (and as $-\infty$ if no such $m$ exists). For a vector bundle $E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, one classical extension defines the Iitaka dimension of $E$ as the Iitaka dimension of the tautological line bundle $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(E)}(1)$ on the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$.

Fix numerical invariants (rank, Chern classes) and a polarization $H$ on $X$, and let $M$ denote the moduli space of Gieseker $H$-semistable coherent sheaves on $X$ with those invariants. Because $\dim X > 1$, the properly semistable locus of $M$ contains points represented by torsion-free (or pure) coherent sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ that are not locally free; in particular the projective bundle construction $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{F})$ does not directly apply.

Problem: Formulate the optimal extension of the notion of Iitaka dimension from vector bundles to arbitrary Gieseker-semistable coherent sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ (including non-locally-free ones), in such a way that:
(i) it agrees with the usual Iitaka dimension $\kappa(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(E)}(1))$ when $\mathcal{F} = E$ is a vector bundle;
(ii) it behaves well in families parameterized by $M$ (e.g. semicontinuity or constancy along $S$-equivalence classes); and
(iii) it captures the asymptotic growth of global sections of symmetric powers (or a suitable replacement, such as reflexive symmetric powers $(\mathrm{Sym}^m \mathcal{F})^{\vee\vee}$) of $\mathcal{F}$.
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found proposing a canonical definition of Iitaka dimension for properly semistable, non-locally-free coherent sheaves on higher-dimensional varieties. Standard references (Huybrechts–Lehn, Wikipedia entries on Iitaka/Kodaira dimension) define Iitaka dimension for line bundles and, via $\mathbb{P}(E)$, for vector bundles, but do not give an accepted extension to the non-locally-free semistable case. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Iitaka dimension - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Defines Iitaka dimension for line bundles via maps to projective space; no extension to non-locally-free sheaves given.
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition is for line bundles; extensions to vector bundles use projectivization, which fails for non-locally-free sheaves.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry of Moduli Spaces of Sheaves (Huybrechts–Lehn)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on moduli of semistable sheaves; treats properly semistable locus but does not provide an Iitaka-dimension theory for non-locally-free semistable sheaves.
status_evidence.claim: No canonical Iitaka dimension is defined for non-locally-free semistable sheaves in the standard reference.
